title: Chicken and Bacon Salad
subtitle: Warm crispy bacon and roasted chicken thighs on cos lettuce with a mustardy dressing
excerpt: Roasted chicken thighs and crispy grilled bacon over cos lettuce with cherry tomatoes and a sharp Dijon dressing. A satisfying main-course salad that eats as a substantial lunch.
sourceNotes: Chicken and bacon salad is a staple of the British pub lunch and gastropub menu, related to but distinct from the American chef's salad and the French salade tiede (warm salad). The combination of warm chicken, crispy bacon and a sharp mustardy vinaigrette on salad leaves is well documented in British bistro and home cooking from the 1990s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the chicken up to 2 hours ahead. Cook the bacon and assemble just before serving.

content.text: Chicken and bacon salad is a proper lunch dish: filling, easy to prepare mostly in advance, and reliable. Chicken thighs rather than breasts are the better choice here because they stay moist and have more flavour. The bacon should be cooked until very crispy so it provides textural contrast to the tender chicken and soft leaves. The mustardy dressing should be sharp enough to cut through both.

Heat the oven to 200 C. Rub {{chicken-thigh}} chicken thighs with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 0.5 tsp of salt. Place skin-side up on a baking tray. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until the skin is golden and the juices run clear. Rest for 5 minutes, then shred the meat off the bone.
Cook {{back-bacon}} of bacon in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat until very crispy. Remove and drain. When cool enough to handle, tear or cut into pieces.

Whisk together {{white-wine-vinegar}} of white wine vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of extra-virgin olive oil, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, 0.25 tsp of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Arrange the cos lettuce on a large plate. Scatter over the cherry tomatoes and spring onion if using. Pile the warm shredded chicken and crispy bacon on top. Drizzle the dressing over. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Thighs overcooked, or used breast meat instead.
items.fix: Thighs are forgiving; breast meat dries out quickly. Remove thighs as soon as the juices run clear. The resting time helps redistribute the juices.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too much fat in the pan.
items.fix: Use a dry pan over high heat. Back bacon needs high heat to crisp; lower heat renders the fat slowly and steams the rasher rather than crisping it.

content.text: Chicken and bacon salad is a mainstay of the British gastropub lunch menu, where it has appeared in various iterations since the early 2000s. It is related to the French salade tiede tradition of serving warm protein on cold leaves, and adapted to British tastes through the addition of back bacon and a mustardy vinaigrette. It is also one of the best uses for leftover roast chicken.
